### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/spec`, touching **1** documentable anchor(s).

**10** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via FilterCondition (symbol, a top-level type))_
- `content/docs/api/data-api.mdx`  _(via FilterCondition (symbol, a top-level type))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx`  _(via FilterCondition (symbol, a top-level type))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/queries.mdx`  _(via FilterCondition (symbol, a top-level type))_
- `content/docs/getting-started/quick-reference.mdx`  _(via FilterCondition (symbol, a top-level type))_
- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx`  _(via FilterCondition (symbol, a top-level type))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/query-syntax.mdx`  _(via FilterCondition (symbol, a top-level type))_
- `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`  _(via FilterCondition (symbol, a top-level type))_
- `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx`  _(via FilterCondition (symbol, a top-level type))_
- `content/docs/ui/dashboards.mdx`  _(via FilterCondition (symbol, a top-level type))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via FilterCondition (symbol, a top-level type))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **174** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a3a74f27020d9da3d15987129ddfb812d522e7a3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ef4df610ac00d973c1be2354000f1d211b856c4e` — the merge of head `38da08ce64242ab60ce9b7159451f45cb027f16c` into base `a3a74f27020d9da3d15987129ddfb812d522e7a3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ef4df610ac00d973c1be2354000f1d211b856c4e && git checkout ef4df610ac00d973c1be2354000f1d211b856c4e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a3a74f27020d9da3d15987129ddfb812d522e7a3 38da08ce64242ab60ce9b7159451f45cb027f16c && git checkout -B drift-repro a3a74f27020d9da3d15987129ddfb812d522e7a3 && git merge --no-ff 38da08ce64242ab60ce9b7159451f45cb027f16c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a3a74f27020d9da3d15987129ddfb812d522e7a3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a3a74f27020d9da3d15987129ddfb812d522e7a3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1: ACCEPT** (L1-a, for area d7-C) at head `3253eff946744e7200b7d922713a02a5662ee8cf`, read 2026-11-19T16:38Z.

Checklist (`l1-review-checklist.md`), each item read on GitHub or in the head tree, not from the report:

- **Shape.** Draft, base `main`, mergeable clean. The only closing keyword is `Fixes #35494`, and it fits: the card asks for the docblock sentences plus a regen of any generated copy, and the PR delivers both (no generated copy exists, see below). No other issue number sits next to a closing verb anywhere in the body.
- **Scope.** One file, `packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts`, +9/−6, TypeScript comment text only: no schema, type or `.describe()` change. No `content/docs/releases/` edit. `Metadata-protocol: none` and `Clause-②: no` are true for a comment-only diff.
- **Changeset.** `@objectstack/spec` is published and ships `src/**/*.zod.ts`, so this corrects shipped text. `skip-changeset` follows this repo's route for comment-only spec PRs (merged precedent: #30643, #31504, #28460, #31055), and `Check Changeset` is `success` at head.
- **Sentences checked against code** (`origin/main` = the head's own tree for these files):
  - "Up to three relationships deep … `RELATION_CONDITION_MAX_HOPS`": `packages/objectql/src/relation-filter-lowering.ts:104` is `= 3`. `admitRelationCondition` starts at `hops = 1` and refuses `hop-limit` only when a relation key holding a condition appears at `hops >= 3` (`:221`), so three relationships are served and a condition beneath a fourth is refused. That is exactly "past the third relationship".
  - "a dotted key, is refused": `:213` `refuse('dotted-key', key)`.
  - "(`INVALID_FILTER` / 400)": `invalidFilterError` in `packages/objectql/src/filter-comparand-shape.ts` sets `code` INVALID_FILTER, `status` 400 and `httpStatus` 400.
  - "ADR-0071's 3-hop limit": the ADR-0071 status line reads "multi-hop to-one joins behind the 3-hop cap", and the constant's docblock names it as that limit.
  - The unchanged "single or multiple" stays true at depth: the recursion carries no to-one restriction past the first hop.
  - The other three edits (the `FilterCondition` member comment, the `QueryFilter` example, the typed `Filter` member comment) say the same limit in one line each.
- **Stale wording sweep.** At head, `packages/spec/src` has no nested-relation "one level" sentence left. The only other repo hit, `packages/lint/src/filter-walk.ts:238`, is about the lint walk's own depth, not a copy of the served-depth claim. I scanned the hand-written `content/docs/**` pages the drift bot listed: none states a nested-relation depth.
- **Tests and gates.** No behaviour change, so no test is owed. The local gate commands are in the body with their exit codes. CI at `3253eff9`: 74 check runs, every one `success` or `skipped`, including `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` (both `success`).
- **Accepted deviation.** The card named three sentences. The PR fixes four, the fourth being the typed `Filter` member comment: same defect, same file, inside the claim surface, and the census command is in `## Acceptance notes`.
- **Out of scope / filings.** None.

**Contract review.** This L1 ACCEPT does not stand in for it. The diff touches `packages/spec/src/**` (non-test), which is the published-schema face, so one `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` L2 is owed at this head. d7-C is running it as an isolated reviewer. Landing waits for a same-shape PASS at `3253eff9`; until that is on record, the dispatching area owes `needs:contract-review` on this PR.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `3253eff946744e7200b7d922713a02a5662ee8cf`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts + none
Security-touching: no

### ① Derived judgments

Readings are taken at the PR head `3253eff9` and, for code outside the diff, at `origin/main` `b65488a8` (the merge base), both in objectstack-ai/objectstack.

- **Accept set: unchanged. Right.** The net diff is one file, 9 insertions and 6 deletions, and every changed line is comment text: lines 2222 to 2227 inside the `FilterCondition` JSDoc, the trailing comments on 2238 and 2467 (the code tokens ahead of each comment are byte-identical), and line 2376 inside the `QueryFilter` example JSDoc. `FilterConditionSchema`, `FieldOperatorsSchema` and both type bodies do not move.
- **Exports and type surface: unchanged. Right.** `TypeScript Type Check`, the job that carries `check:api-surface`, `check:docs` and `check:authorable-surface`, is `success` on this head.
- **Generated reference docs: none owed. Right.** The four sentences are TypeScript comments, not `.describe()` text. No page under `content/docs/references/` carries the old sentence at `b65488a8`, and `check:docs` is green with nothing regenerated. The second half of the card's Done-when has nothing to regenerate.
- **Published prose: it moves. Right as a change, and it is what ② turns on.** `packages/spec/package.json` at `b65488a8` lists `src/**/*.zod.ts` in `files[]` and the package is not private, so `src/data/filter.zod.ts` ships verbatim in the `@objectstack/spec` tarball. The new sentences replace "one level" there.
- **The stated limit: right.** `RELATION_CONDITION_MAX_HOPS = 3` at `packages/objectql/src/relation-filter-lowering.ts:104`. `admitRelationCondition` (:185) enters at `hops = 1` and refuses `hop-limit` at :221 when a relation key holds a condition of its own once `hops` has reached the constant. So `{ a: { b: { c: { field: v } } } }` is admitted and a condition beneath a fourth relationship is refused.
- **The stated refusal: right.** Every relation-arm refusal, `hop-limit` and `dotted-key` included, leaves the `where` door through `refuse()` at `packages/objectql/src/number-comparand-declared-type-door.ts:647`, which throws `invalidFilterError` (`packages/objectql/src/filter-comparand-shape.ts:84`: code `INVALID_FILTER`, status 400).
- **The ADR cite: right.** ADR-0071 Decision reads "A depth cap (default **3 hops** → 4 objects, Salesforce-report-type parity) bounds join count/perf", and the constant's own docblock names itself that hop limit. "Relationships" is the accurate noun: the admission counts a multi-valued relation as a hop too, where ADR-0071's dataset path is to-one only.
- **Census: right.** At the head, the four edited sentences are the only statements of nested-relation depth in `filter.zod.ts`. The one remaining "one level" hit (line 2619) is about a group key and a field key in one filter node, not relations.

Not judged, noted for the author: the PR body says the refusal is thrown through `relationConditionError`. That export has no caller outside tests at `b65488a8`; the door throws through `refuse()` as above. The envelope is the same and the docblock does not name the function.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: no` is right. No key lands on a published payload and no accept set moves.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is right. That kind takes `patch`.
- **M1 (must-fix) — `skip-changeset` does not match what the diff publishes: a `patch` changeset on `@objectstack/spec` is owed.**
  - The one changed file is shipped as source (① above), so this diff changes bytes of a released package.
  - AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist step 3: "A bug fix in a released package takes a **`patch`** changeset — never none, and ⛔ never `skip-changeset`: that label is for a diff that publishes nothing from any released package." Triage graded this card a Bug at p2 on exactly that ground (comment 7009555753: "a wrong sentence in shipped text is a Bug at that reach").
  - `.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/references/l1-review-checklist.md` lines 26, 29 and 30 say the same in the seat's own words: 「已发布 = 各包 `files[]` 实际发运的内容;spec 发运 `src/**/*.zod.ts`,假 TSDoc/`.describe()` 即缺陷」, 「每个被触及的包,`private: false` 即已发布 ⇒ 读 `package.json` 核 changeset 在不在」, 「⛔ 判据不是改动大小,也不是用户可见的感觉判断;⛔ 缺了不入队」.
  - The rule the dev followed is `.claude/agents/os-dev.md` line 301, whose fast lane lists comments as not published. That holds where `files[]` ships only built JavaScript. It does not hold for this glob, line 300 of the same file defines published as what `files[]` ships, and AGENTS.md outranks it.
  - Precedent runs both ways and does not decide it. Comment-only edits to a spec `*.zod.ts` file landed under the label in merged PRs 31055 and 28460. The same kind of edit took a spec `patch` in the pending `.changeset/34824-action-refusals-skill.md` ("two comment-only edits in packages/spec") and in released entries of `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md`: lines 1872 to 1877 in 18.5.0 ("TSDoc only … `@objectstack/spec` ships `src/**/*.zod.ts` itself, so they publish"), and lines 39594, 39858 and 39901 (each "shipped, which is why it carries a changeset rather than `skip-changeset`").
  - `Check Changeset` is `success` on this head only because the label exempts the job. Its own text leaves a wrong label to review.
  - Remedy: add `.changeset/35494-nested-relation-hop-docblock.md` naming `'@objectstack/spec': patch`, with `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` in its body and one or two sentences saying the form 4 docblock now states the three-relationship limit. Take the `skip-changeset` label off, so that `Check Changeset` judges the new entry. The delta review reads that one file.

Worth a card of its own in the `.claude/**` lane: `os-dev.md` line 301 and `l1-review-checklist.md` line 26 give opposite answers for a comment in a spec `*.zod.ts` file.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`: empty.** Nothing to answer.
- **Deviation 1, four sentences where the card named three: right.** The fourth (the typed `Filter` member comment, 2464 on main) said the same false thing. Leaving it would have left the file contradicting itself, and it is inside the claim's file surface.
- **Deviation 2, nothing regenerated: right.** See ①.
- **Out-of-scope finding, "the same on every driver" (form 4 docblock, line 2217): answered, and escalated for a card.**
  - Not touched by this diff. The changed lines are 2222 to 2227, 2238, 2376 and 2467, and line 2217 reads the same at `b65488a8` and at the head.
  - Not made newly false. It was already false at `b65488a8`: `packages/spec/src/data/driver.zod.ts:454` to 462 and `relationReadDriverRefusal` (`relation-filter-lowering.ts:370`) refuse a single-valued relation condition on a read verb, `INVALID_FILTER` / 400, on a driver that does not declare `readableIdsLeaf` (MongoDB, OData).
  - The dev's disposition, "not a filable class", does not hold. It is a false TSDoc sentence in a shipped `*.zod.ts` file, which `l1-review-checklist.md` line 26 calls a defect, and line 28 gives the route for one that is noticed and not touched: 「只注意到、未触碰的立卡不修,记明已发布面」. Evidence for the card is contract text: two docblocks of the same published package contradict each other, and the hand-written page `content/docs/kernel/contracts/data-engine.mdx` already reads "the same on every driver that serves it (below)" at line 192 and states the refusal at line 225. Same class and reach as this card, `domain:spec`, `area:data`.
  - The same card can carry the cap sentence at head lines 2227 to 2229, "A condition matching more related records than the engine's cap is refused rather than truncated". It holds only where ids are read. On the subquery path of a read verb nothing is capped (`relation-filter-lowering.ts:34` to 44). This diff re-wrapped that sentence and did not reword it.
  - Not fixed here: the card's Done-when is the hop limit, and the true sentence about drivers is conditional on verb, relation arity and the driver bit, so it is not a mechanical in-place fix.
- **`security_findings: "withheld"`.** Not answerable from this record's inputs. No changed line teaches permission, sharing, credential, token or authentication behaviour: the docblock's sentences about reading as the caller, row scope and field permissions are on unchanged lines 2217 to 2221. Hence `Security-touching: no`.
- **SQL push-down: not applicable.** No code line changes, so there is no new id materialisation and no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/data/filter.zod.ts`: the four sentences hold against the code they cite and against the first consumer.**

- Form 4 docblock (2222 to 2227), clause by clause against `admitRelationCondition`: "up to three relationships deep" is the constant; "a relation key may hold a condition of its own" is the recursion at :222; "a condition past the third relationship, or a dotted key, is refused (`INVALID_FILTER` / 400)" is `hop-limit` at :221 and `dotted-key` at :213 through the envelope in ①. Naming `RELATION_CONDITION_MAX_HOPS` and its file meets the card's "and where it is enforced", in the symbol-in-path form `check:spec-docblock-symbol-anchors` resolves (`Lint & Repo Gates` is `success`).
- The three one-line comments (2238, 2376, 2467) state the same number and point back to form 4. "Typed at any depth here" on the typed `Filter` member is true of the recursive type.
- First consumer, the dashboard drill the card names: `DATASET_DRILL_MAX_HOPS = 3` at `ui/packages/core/src/utils/dataset-format.ts:781`, one nesting level per hop. What the drill sends at its deepest is what the docblock now says is served.
- Tried to break it, and could not:
  - A deeper chain cannot hide under `$and` inside a nested condition. An object with a `$` key is not the nested-relation form (`isNoOperatorObject`), so the admission never recurses through one.
  - A relation key beneath a top-level `$and`, `$or` or `$not` is admitted from `hops = 1`, the same as a bare one.
  - Each hop's related read re-admits only the remainder of the condition, which is shallower, so no path reaches a fourth relationship.
  - No other depth cap sits under three: the filter walks stop at depth 32 (`PRESET_WALK_MAX_DEPTH` at `filter.zod.ts:1969`, and `number-comparand-declared-type-door.ts:499`).
- **N1 (nit) — "every key must be a field the related object declares" understates the accept set.** The clause is carried verbatim into the rewritten sentence. The admission also takes the platform-provisioned `id`, `created_at` and `updated_at` (`relation-filter-lowering.ts:216`). It promises nothing the engine refuses, and the docs page has the same clause at line 205. Accepted deviation; it may ride the M1 commit or be left.

Implementing files in the diff: none. The engine files above are outside the diff: read, not reviewed.

④ raises no blocking finding of its own. M1 in ② is the round's one blocking finding.
